title: ARIA Roles & Practical Accessibility 🛠️
description: When HTML isn't enough: use ARIA attributes to fill gaps, and how to test accessibility.

slides.title: What is ARIA? 🦾
slides.content:
# Accessible Rich Internet Applications

ARIA is a set of attributes that supplement HTML semantics when native elements can't express the desired interaction. It doesn't add new functionality – it provides information to assistive technologies.

**First rule of ARIA:** Don't use ARIA if you can use a native HTML element that already provides the semantics and behaviour (like `<button>` instead of `<div role="button">`).

slides.title: Common ARIA Attributes 🏷️
slides.content:
# Roles, States, and Properties

- `role` – defines what an element is (e.g., `role="banner"`, `role="navigation"`).
- `aria-label` – provides an accessible name (e.g., for a button with no visible text).
- `aria-labelledby` – points to another element that serves as the label.
- `aria-describedby` – provides additional description.
- `aria-hidden="true"` – hides an element from screen readers (decorative).

Example:
```html
<button aria-label="Close dialog">X</button>
```

quizData.question: What is the correct use of `aria-label`?

options.text: To change the visual appearance of an element
To provide an accessible name for an element when visible text is not present or sufficient

quizData.explanation: `aria-label` gives a text label for assistive technology, overriding any inherent label.

slides.title: Live Regions & Dynamic Content 🔄
slides.content:
# Announcing Changes Without Page Refresh For content that updates dynamically (like a chat message or form error), use `aria-live` to inform screen readers: - `aria-live="polite"` – announces when user is idle. - `aria-live="assertive"` – interrupts immediately. ```html
Message sent!
``` Update the inner content; the screen reader will announce it.

slides.title: Testing Accessibility 🧪
slides.content:
# Tools You Can Use

- **Keyboard only:** unplug your mouse and navigate your site. Can you reach everything?
- **Screen readers:** NVDA (Windows), VoiceOver (Mac), TalkBack (Android).
- **Browser extensions:** axe DevTools, Lighthouse (Chrome), WAVE.
- **Automated tests:** axe‑core for CI/CD.

Manual testing is crucial; automated tools catch only ~30% of issues.

slides.title: A 'Skip to Content' Link
slides.content: An essential accessibility feature – let keyboard users bypass navigation:
slides.codeSnippet:
Skip to main content
... navigation ...

Welcome

quizData.question: Which ARIA attribute hides an element from screen readers?
quizData.explanation: `aria-hidden="true"` removes the element from the accessibility tree.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## No ARIA Is Better Than Bad ARIA

Incorrect ARIA can make a site *less* accessible. If you're unsure, stick to native HTML elements – they come with correct implicit ARIA roles.
